This is the empirical companion to the Axiom of Consent, which derives a consent-friction functional F = σ(1+ε)/(1+α) from a single axiom and leaves its adequacy open. We test that functional in a four-agent shared-resource MARL environment—a 5×5×5 factorial of 125 conditions, 30 independent replications each—3,750 Independent Q-Learning (IQL) training runs, with an additive value-decomposition learner (VDN) re-run alongside on reduced control grids—and report two things: an honest characterization of which of its variables survive, and a methodological control battery showing how design choices manufacture spurious coordination findings. The kernel variables matter directionally, but the specific monotone form is rejected as a single-index predictor on comparative grounds (an independent-effects model decisively beats it; on the signed re-test the form itself clears the pre-registered absolute fit bar for VDN).
